etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English conneccioun, connexioun, conneccyon, conneccion, from Latin connexionem (nominative connexio (“a conclusion, binding together”)), from connectō, an alternative spelling of cōnectō (“I bind together”), from compound of co- (“together”) and nectō (“I bind”).

In American English mid-18c., spelling shifted from connexion to connection (equivalent to connect +‎ -ion), thus making connexion British dated and connection in international use.

definitions.definition: The point at which two or more things are connected.

quote.citation: 2004 April 15, “Morning swoop in hunt for Jodi's killer”, in The Scotsman‎[1]:
quote.text: A spokesman for Lothian and Borders Police said: "We can confirm that a 15-year-old boy has been arrested and charged in connection with the murder of Jodi Jones. A 45-year-old has also been arrested in connection with allegations of attempting to pervert the course of justice. A report on this has been sent to the procurator fiscal."

definitions.definition: A feeling of understanding and ease of communication between two or more people.
An established communications or transportation link.
(transport) A transfer from one transportation vehicle to another in scheduled transportation service.

quote.citation: 2022 January 12, Paul Bigland, “Fab Four: the nation's finest stations: Eastbourne”, in RAIL, number 948, page 26:
quote.text: It is kept super-clean by helpful staff who still find the time to help customers with tight connections.

definitions.definition: A person related to oneself, through either family or business.

(mathematics) A set of sets that contains the empty set, all one-element sets for any element that is included in any of the sets, and the union of any group of sets that are elements where the intersections of those sets is non-empty.
(religion) A Methodist denomination as a whole, as opposed to its constituent churches, circuits, districts and conferences.

quote.citation: 1927, Havelock Ellis, Studies in the Psychology of Sex, Volume 2 (of 6)‎[2]:
quote.text: The exact nature of the relations between the boy-wife and his protector are doubtful; they certainly have connection, but the natives repudiate with horror and disgust the idea of sodomy.

quote.citation: 1957, Jack Kerouac, On the Road, Viking Press, →OCLC:
quote.text: Now the final study was the drug habit. He was now in New Orleans, slipping along the streets with shady characters and haunting connection bars.
